desc:
A delivery network has n depots labelled 0 to n - 1. Each edges[i] = [from, to, cost] is a one-way route. A cost can be negative: the courier receives a rebate for that leg.

It is guaranteed that no cycle in the network has a negative total cost, so cheapest routes are well defined. Return an array dist of length n where dist[v] is the lowest total cost of a route from src to depot v, or 1000000000 if v cannot be reached from src. Of course dist[src] = 0.

Example: n = 5, edges = [[0,1,4],[0,2,5],[1,2,-3],[2,3,2],[3,1,2]], src = 0. Going 0 → 1 → 2 costs 4 - 3 = 1, cheaper than the direct 5. The answer is [0, 4, 1, 3, 1000000000]; depot 4 has no incoming route.
constraints: edges[i] = [from, to, cost] with 0 ≤ from, to < n, from ≠ to and -1,000 ≤ cost ≤ 1,000
Each ordered pair (from, to) appears at most once
The graph has no cycle of negative total cost; zero-cost cycles may exist
hints: Dijkstra's greedy choice (the closest unfinished node is final) fails once an edge can lower a cost that was already settled.
A cheapest route never needs to repeat a depot, so it has at most n - 1 edges. Relax every edge repeatedly: dist[v] = min(dist[v], dist[u] + cost).

Bellman-Ford: do up to n - 1 passes over all edges, skipping edges whose source is still unreachable, and stop early when a whole pass changes nothing. After pass j, every route with at most j edges is accounted for.
editorial: Bellman-Ford keeps the best known cost for each depot and relaxes all edges again and again. Induction on the number of edges shows that after pass j, dist[v] is at most the cost of the cheapest route to v that uses j edges or fewer. Because there is no negative cycle, a cheapest route can be chosen without repeated depots, so n - 1 edges and therefore n - 1 passes always suffice.

Each pass costs O(E), so the total is O(n · E) in the worst case, and the early exit makes typical inputs much faster. Only relax from depots that are already reachable; adding a cost to a 'not reachable' marker would corrupt the result. Dijkstra is faster (O(E log n)) but only correct for non-negative costs. Adding a constant to every edge to remove negatives does not work either, since routes with more edges would be penalised more.
